stem.text: Hydrated cobalt(II) sulfate loses water when heated to give anhydrous cobalt(II) sulfate. All the water of crystallisation is lost to the atmosphere as steam.
When $3.10\ \text{g}$ of hydrated cobalt(II) sulfate, $\text{CoSO}_4\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is heated to constant mass the **loss** in mass is $1.39\ \text{g}$.
What is the value of $x$, to the nearest whole number?
